grade.rationale: The parser validates the core review structure well, including grades, aspect references, severities, positions, and provenance restrictions. However, several malformed JSON shapes are either silently accepted or escape through unexpected exception types, and location ranges are not checked for logical ordering.

summary: Core validation is clear and reasonably maintainable, but error handling is inconsistent for non-object nodes, optional properties can bypass type validation, and inverted source ranges are accepted. Build analyzer evidence reported no .NET findings; test coverage remains unknown.

grade.rationale: Most required fields and value constraints are validated, but malformed optional properties and reversed location ranges can pass validation.
Invalid node shapes do not consistently produce ReviewResponseException, weakening the parser's error contract for untrusted responses.
The implementation is compact and uses focused validation helpers, though repeated conditional type checks make validation semantics inconsistent.
Control flow and validation intent are generally easy to follow, with descriptive domain-specific error messages.
The parser is deterministic and side-effect free, but its inconsistent exception behavior complicates precise negative-case assertions. Coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Non-object JSON roots escape the parser's exception contract
findings.description: JsonNode.AsObject() throws InvalidOperationException when the parsed root is an array or scalar, but the catch block handles only JsonException. Consequently, valid JSON with the wrong shape does not produce the documented domain-specific ReviewResponseException. The same AsObject pattern is also used for nested aspects, findings, locations, and thread updates.
findings.recommendation: Check node types with pattern matching, such as `node is JsonObject root`, or catch and wrap InvalidOperationException at the parsing boundary. Apply the same approach to nested object elements so every malformed response consistently raises ReviewResponseException.

findings.title: Optional properties accept null, arrays, and objects
findings.description: The fingerprint and status validators run only when the property value is a JsonValue. If either property is present as null, an array, or an object, its validation is skipped and the malformed response is accepted.
findings.recommendation: When an optional property is present, require it to be a JsonValue containing a string before validating its allowed format or values. Distinguish property absence from a present value of the wrong JSON type.

findings.title: Malformed threadUpdates values are silently ignored
findings.description: Thread updates are validated only when the property happens to be a JsonArray. A present null, string, number, or object is treated the same as an absent property, allowing an invalid top-level response shape to pass.
findings.recommendation: If the root contains `threadUpdates`, require its value to be a JsonArray and reject every other JSON type. Skip validation only when the property is genuinely absent.

findings.title: Location ranges may end before they start
findings.description: Start and end positions are independently checked for positive line and column values, but their relative ordering is never validated. The parser therefore accepts impossible ranges whose end precedes their start.
findings.recommendation: After validating both positions, compare them lexicographically by line and then column, rejecting a range when its end is earlier than its start.
